questions.question: What does go mod tidy do in Go?
questions.title: Go Mod Tidy
questions.direct_answer: Reconciles go.mod with the code's actual imports: adds missing dependencies, removes unused ones, updates go.sum. The reflex command — run it after adding or removing imports.

sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: Reconciles go.mod with the code's actual imports: adds missing dependencies, removes unused ones, updates go.sum. The reflex command — run it after adding or removing imports.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The reconciliation, executed:

Before: go.mod has no requires
After importing uuid and running go mod tidy:
```
go: downloading github.com/google/uuid v1.6.0
```
go.mod now has:
```
require github.com/google/uuid v1.6.0
```
go.sum now has the hashes. (Verified.)

What tidy does, precisely:
1. Scans ALL Go files in the module — the actual import statements
2. Resolves each external import to a module + version (MVS)
3. Adds missing requires, removes requires nothing imports
4. Downloads and verifies (updates go.sum)
5. Cleans: drops test-only and build-constrained requires when they're no longer referenced

The idiom: go mod tidy is the reflex after adding or removing imports. It's idempotent (running twice = same result). CI runs it and checks the diff is empty — the discipline that catches forgotten updates.

What it does NOT: upgrade versions (that's go get -u), run any code, or pick 'latest' (it keeps existing versions unless an import requires a newer one).

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CMD[go mod tidy] --> SCAN[scan all imports]
    SCAN --> DIFF[compare vs go.mod requires]
    DIFF --> ADD[add missing]
    DIFF --> REMOVE[remove unused]
    ADD --> MVS[resolve versions]
    MVS --> SUM[download + verify + update go.sum]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The import-to-module resolution, mechanically: each import path maps to a module by finding the longest prefix that's a module root (github.com/org/repo/subpackage → module github.com/org/repo). tidy queries the proxy for available versions, runs MVS, and pins the result.

The go.sum update: each resolved module version is downloaded, hashed (the go.sum entries are dirhash + modhash + modfile hash), and recorded. Subsequent builds verify against these hashes — the supply-chain integrity that go.sum provides.

The CI check pattern: `go mod tidy && git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum` — the diff-is-empty assertion in a pipeline. Any drift (a dependency someone added without tidying) breaks CI, keeping the files always-clean.
